title: SLA-simulated-usage-preview-playbook-for-ad-hoc-analytics-requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create an operational playbook and automated triage flow that gives customer-facing teams and self-serve users a fast, risk-aware estimate for (1) expected SLA/latency impact, (2) per-run and monthly cost envelope, and (3) a PII-safe sample preview for on-demand analytics/export requests. This should reduce engineering handoffs for high-touch asks and provide deterministic routing into three lanes: self-serve (console/template), assisted (PM/SE), and eng-backed (sustained custom delivery).

Scope: Ad-hoc usage analytics requests coming from Console 'Request Insights' flow, partner success emails, and Solutions/SE intake. Focus on non-bug asks: CSV/Parquet exports, pre-built dashboards, tenant-slice snapshots, and cost/latency-sensitive query sandboxes. Excludes: long-running ETL pipelines, custom connector engineering, and regulatory compliance audits (seek Security/Legal separately).

What we will deliver: A documented playbook + automated triage-bot that runs lightweight SLA simulations against sampled telemetry to estimate p95 latency and throughput impact; cost-forecast calculator that uses historical token/row distribution and current pricing to produce three risk bands (low/medium/high); PII-safe sample preview generator that applies deterministic redaction and synthetic sampling rules for preview payloads; routing matrix that maps maturity score -> delivery lane and SLA.

Why: Field teams currently open ad-hoc tickets that require multiple synchronous clarifications and engineering time. Providing an upfront simulated forecast and a sample preview will speed decisions, set expectations with customers, and reduce unnecessary eng cycles while preserving safety and privacy.

Success metrics: median time-to-response (target < 48 hours) for intake; percent of ad-hoc asks resolved without eng intervention (target 60% within three months); accuracy of cost forecast (within ±20% for 75% of sampled requests); reduction in rework due to PII exposure (target 0 incidents from preview flow).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Triage form added to Console with fields required for automated scoring (query template, expected row range, time window, export format, tenant tier, SLA requirement). 2) Automation runs SLA simulation using recent telemetry and returns p50/p95 latency and an estimated token/row cost band. 3) System produces a PII-safe sample preview (first N rows) with redaction/synthesis applied and explicit note of what was removed. 4) Routing decision produced with clear owner and ETA. 5) Documented playbook and runbook for support/SE/PM. 6) Telemetry captured in dashboards for monitoring adoption and forecast accuracy.
steps: 1) Define intake form schema and minimal required fields. 2) Prototype lightweight SLA simulator using sampled traces + conservative concurrency model. 3) Build cost forecast model using historical usage buckets and current pricing tiers; include burst/flat-rate adjustments. 4) Specify PII redaction and synthetic-sample rules with Security. 5) Implement triage-bot prototype (internal Slack + Console webhook) that accepts intake payload and returns simulation + preview + routing. 6) Run pilot with two enterprise customers and Solutions team. 7) Iterate on thresholds and update playbook, automate dashboards. 8) Expand to self-serve Console lane once pilot stable.
decisions: - Use conservative p95 estimator instead of mean to avoid underpromising. - Preview sample limited to 100 rows or 10KB unredacted, whichever is smaller; apply redaction-first policy. - Three lanes (self-serve, assisted, eng-backed) and automated escalation at 48h if unresolved. - Cost forecast uses 3 bands derived from 10/50/90 percentile historical scenarios for tenant similar size.
